content.title: IF YOU ATE {{THIS}} EVERY DAY... HERE'S WHAT YOUR BODY DOES
facts: If you ate **sardines** every day for 3 weeks, your joints would feel less stiff in the morning as the omega-3s calm inflammation around them.
If you ate **beef liver** every day for 10 days, your energy would stabilize and that 3pm crash would fade, thanks to a flood of B12 and easily absorbed iron.
If you ate **kimchi** every day for 2 weeks, your bloating would ease up as its live bacteria crowd out the gas-producing microbes in your gut.
If you ate **sunflower seeds** every day for 30 days, your skin would look slightly smoother from the vitamin E protecting it against daily oxidative stress.
If you ate **lentils** every day for 1 week, your hunger would stop spiking between meals as their fiber and protein slow digestion way down.
If you ate **oysters** every day for 2 weeks (if you can stomach it), your wound healing and immune response would sharpen up from the massive zinc dose.
If you ate **dark chocolate (85%+)** every day for 2 weeks, your blood pressure could nudge down slightly as flavanols help your blood vessels relax.
If you ate **figs** every day for 10 days, you'd likely notice more regular digestion as their fiber and natural sugars get things moving gently.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
Small daily swaps add up faster than people think. Take **sardines** — the omega-3s in them don't just sit there, they actually get built into your joint tissue and dial down the inflammatory chemicals your body releases when things get irritated. **Kimchi** works differently: it's a live culture, so every bite is dropping beneficial bacteria into your gut that compete with the species linked to excess gas and bloating, which is why people often notice a calmer stomach within days. And **oysters**, despite the ick factor for some, are one of the densest natural sources of zinc, a mineral your immune cells and skin cells both depend on to repair themselves quickly. Everyone's body is different, so give it time and listen to yours.
